question.problem:
Consider the orthogonal set $U$ below. By adding a new vector $x=[{x}_{1},\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}]^{T},$ extend the set so that it forms an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}.$ What is the value of $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}}?$

$$
U=\{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $U$ as ${u}_{1},\,{u}_{2}.$ To extend the given set to an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}$, we need to find a third vector $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ such that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot x=0 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot x=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+-2{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system above and reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{4}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{5}{2} & -\frac{3}{4} & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-\frac{3}{10}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+2(-\frac{3}{10}{x}_{3})+3{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=(-\frac{3}{5}){x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{5}{x}_{3} \\ -\frac{3}{10}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=10,$ we obtain the vector 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3 \\ 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}$ is

$$
\{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Finally, $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}}=\frac{-6}{-3}=2.$
